conclusion: A fresh selected entry that also serves a retained child keeps the child as the durable next scheduling hint, while its dispatch and receipt remain bound to the entry and its original scheduling kind still pays the fairness quota.

newCases: Fresh necessary entry persists its actual child before dispatch without transferring the entry receipt or resetting fairness
Unknown entry receipt remains unknown and blocks continuation without completing either child
No-attempt rejection restores the prior selection, cursor and fairness count
Explicit reentry preserves the selected child when multiple children share the entry

limits: Pure runtime tests use supplied route permission and attempt facts; no browser, service or database is created.
Scheduling metadata does not establish arrival, historical target correspondence, replay authority or child completion.
This patch does not fix the Main menu decision ordering or the instance-bound Convert target correspondence gap.
No new live acceptance, recovery latency result or A/B behavior claim is made.
